short_title: ApoB vs LDL-C and non-HDL-C discordance (UK Biobank)

citation.title: Discordance among apoB, non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides: implications for cardiovascular prevention

access.full_text_source: PubMed Central full-text XML (NCBI efetch, PMC11242442); Figure 2 image inspected

study.design_detail: UK Biobank prospective cohort. Distribution of apoB at pre-specified LDL-C, non-HDL-C and triglyceride levels; 10-year Kaplan-Meier ASCVD rates for high vs low apoB within narrow bands of those levels; Cox models with regression residuals (discordance analysis), HRs per 1 SD.
study.population: UK Biobank adults aged 40-73 years, 42% men, free of cardiovascular disease and not on lipid-lowering therapy at baseline; triglycerides < 400 mg/dL, LDL-C < 250 mg/dL
study.setting: United Kingdom, recruited 2006-2010 from primary care lists
study.exposure_or_intervention: Baseline apoB, LDL-C, non-HDL-C, triglycerides (single baseline measurement each)
study.comparator: apoB at least 1 SD above vs at least 1 SD below the mean at fixed (+/-10 mg/dL) LDL-C, non-HDL-C or triglyceride levels; residual (discordant) apoB vs residual LDL-C/non-HDL-C/triglycerides in Cox models
outcomes: New-onset atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), defined in the paper's Supplementary Table S1

findings_summary: In 293 876 UK Biobank adults without cardiovascular disease, apoB correlated very highly with LDL-C and non-HDL-C (r = .96), yet at any fixed LDL-C the apoB values spanned a wide range (for example about 85.8 to 108.8 mg/dL at LDL-C 130 mg/dL, capturing ~95% of people). Within narrow LDL-C, non-HDL-C and triglyceride bands, people with high apoB had higher 10-year ASCVD rates than people with low apoB (for example 7.3 vs 4.0 at LDL-C 130 ± 10 mg/dL). In residual (discordance) models, the part of apoB not explained by LDL-C or non-HDL-C remained associated with ASCVD (HR 1.06 and 1.04 per SD), whereas the part of LDL-C or non-HDL-C not explained by apoB did not (HR 0.99 and 1.00).

limitations.text: Single-country cohort (UK); racial and ethnic subgroups represent that country only.
Observational associations from single baseline measurements. They do not show that lowering apoB specifically, rather than LDL-C, changes outcomes.
People on lipid-lowering therapy at baseline were excluded, so the findings describe untreated lipid levels.

The authors report that the high vs low apoB differences in 10-year rates were statistically significant except at the lowest LDL-C and non-HDL-C levels, which limits what the band comparison says for people with low LDL-C.
The main text does not state whether 'apoB at least 1 SD above/below the mean' uses the cohort apoB distribution or the distribution within each lipid band, and does not report the group sizes.
The 10-year rates are reported without a stated unit; the high and low apoB groups are the tails (beyond ±1 SD), so most people fall between them.
The per-SD hazard ratios for residual apoB are modest (1.04–1.06); a statistically clear residual association is not the same as a large difference in absolute risk for a given person.
Supplementary material (outcome definitions, sensitivity bands, Figure S2, reclassification Table S6) was not reviewed for this record.

applicability_constraints: Adults aged 40–73 at baseline, without cardiovascular disease and not on lipid-lowering therapy.
Triglycerides < 400 mg/dL, LDL-C < 250 mg/dL, apoB 20–400 mg/dL (exclusions).
Cohort event rates describe groups in UK Biobank over 10 years; they are not an individual's risk.

discrepancies.description: Sample size is 293 876 in the Abstract and Table 1 but 293 883 in the Methods text.
The Abstract gives the residual-apoB HR after accounting for LDL-C as 1.06 (95% CI 1.0–1.07); Table 2 and the Results text give 1.06 (1.04, 1.07).
The Discussion states the apoB range at LDL-C 70 mg/dL spans 'an absolute difference of 27.2 mg/dL'; the reported bounds (40.8 to 67.0 mg/dL) differ by 26.2 mg/dL.
discrepancies.handling: Record reports the bounds and our own arithmetic (26.2), labelled as derived.

discrepancies.description: Units are printed as 'md/dL' for two ranges in the Results text.
discrepancies.handling: Treated as a typographical error for mg/dL; quotes kept verbatim.

discrepancies.description: The Results give the apoB SD (22.7 mg/dL) for this UK Biobank cohort; the Discussion describes 22.7 mg/dL as '1 SD of apoB for the American population'.
discrepancies.handling: Record treats 22.7 mg/dL as the UK Biobank cohort SD, per the Results.

interpretation: The paper supports a specific, limited point: two markers that correlate at r = .96 across a population can still disagree substantially for an individual, and in this cohort the disagreement carried prognostic information in the direction of apoB. It does not establish how often the disagreement would change a decision for a given person, and it does not test apoB-guided care. For this project, it is a reason to record apoB alongside LDL-C and non-HDL-C when it is available, and to treat an apparent stability of LDL-C as incomplete information about apoB-containing particles.
